Interestingly enough most of us don’t communicate on our smartphones by calling. We either text or use one of the instant messaging apps, or we check our emails. While your emails will undoubtedly receive plenty of spam messages, it is important to use an app that makes replying to those important emails easier.

So, what are the good email apps for Android? Here is our selection of five of the best ones you should be using right now.

K-9 Mail

If you are a hardcore Android fan, then you might want to pick K-9 Mail for your phone. It’s the original alternative for Gmail on Android and completely developed by the community. You can contribute to the development as well if you want.

Now, the email app supports a lot of functions that make it a superb app. You have IMAP email support, multi-folder synchronisation, filing options, bcc-self and PGP capabilities and Exchange 2003/2007 support. Indeed, if you like to have that extra layer of security to ensure your emails are safe, K-9 Mail is a good pick. It used Public Key Encryption and it lets you encrypt your messages and files – you will have your emails protected by an additional password and this will be useful for people with sensitive information in their email.

WeMail

WeMail is definitely an email client with a difference. Your emails won’t be organised as individual thoughts and emails but rather a chat-like experience. This has the potential to reduce the size of your inbox and you don’t need to keep scrolling down just to find an email from the previous week.

It isn’t any wonder the advanced search function in the app is superb. It’s not only fast but also allows you to find things based on rather little information. For those that hate writing emails, WeMail comes with a well-functioning dictating feature to help you dictate your emails instead of typing them.

Boxer

For those looking something outside of the radar, Boxer is definitely a worth app to check out. It supports email clients like Gmail, Exchange, Yahoo, iCloud and IMAP/POP3 email accounts. You can also integrate it with Dropbox and Evernote. If you need a to-do list feature, this one has it as well.

Boxer’s best feature is the depth in shortcuts. You have handy shortcuts to move items to trash and to block emails, for example. You have 12 options for additional customisation within the email app – you don’t even need to type all the responses but simply click on the pre-configured messages.

There are three versions available: Boxer for Exchange, Boxer Pro and Boxer Pro + Exchange. The Pro version is for those looking for multiple account support and customised quick replies. The Exchange versions add Exchange support automatically via the ActiveSync function.

Microsoft Outlook

For something familiar and easy to use, Microsoft Outlook email app is not a bad option. It’s a sleek, web-based app that offers support and synchronisation with other apps such as Microsoft Exchange, Office 265, Yahoo Mail and so on.

The best feature is the Focused Inbox function. This keeps your most important messages at the top of the screen, making it impossible to forget about these crucial emails. It can be a lifesaver for those using a work email on their smartphone. The calendar support is a big plus as well.

Gmail

Finally, you don’t necessarily have to start downloading a new app on your phone. Each Android smartphone comes with one of the best and most used email app of all time: Gmail. Although the email service launched as an invitation-only service in 2004, it has been open for anyone to use since 2007.

Gmail’s big benefit is the storage – you receive 15GB of free storage from the start. It also supports non-Gmail accounts so you can use Outlook, Yahoo Mail and almost any other IMAP/POP email service with it. Setting up folders for different emails isn’t difficult and you can even have your automated vacation responder.

If you are using a Google account – and chances are you are – then it might be the best to stick to Gmail. It’s already on your phone, it’s easy to use and you don’t need to play with any tricks to make the most out of it. However, if you’re not a fan of Google or you simply want something different, the other four on the list are worthy of checking out.
